source.title: Trusted Loss Correction for Noisy Multi-Label Learning
source.authors: Amirmasoud Ghiassi; Cosmin Octavian Pene; R. Birke; L. Chen

page_placements.theme: Generalization peaks and stopping rules depend on training conditions

record.tranche_reason: Reports results on deep networks trained with corrupted labels, including performance across noise fractions and training epochs. It uses multi-label classification measures and a loss-correction method rather than testing the original random-label fitting recipe.
record.gate_note: Results on noisy-label robustness and training dynamics bear on V4 and V6. The paper does not test completely random labels, unstructured inputs, the stated regularizers, or random-label training time. Cited results and the motivation figure are not extracted as this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the memorization account to motivate and evaluate noise mitigation. Its own results measure clean-test classification performance, not fitting of corrupted training labels or the order in which clean and noisy labels are learned. Increasing test degradation alone does not establish V4's joint training-fit and generalization effect; early test peaks do not establish V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. TLCM uses trusted multi-label and single-label data to estimate a corruption matrix and improve robustness. Across three datasets it outperforms ASL and MPVAE under 30% and 60% corruption. This conclusion concerns clean-test performance, not demonstrated fitting of random labels.
record.recipe_differences: Multi-label image classification with symmetric label corruption and trusted loss correction using gold data; it does not reproduce the random-label training setup in the cited original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and noise fraction affect performance; trusted-data fraction affects results; training epoch changes performance and the peak epoch differs between TLCM and ASL.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-test classification performance declines with increasing label noise, while trusted loss correction improves robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-label classifiers lose clean-test accuracy under symmetric label corruption, and trusted loss correction reduces that loss.

fits_no_version.finding: At 40% noise, TLCM and ASL improve early and then lose test mAP; MPVAE improves toward a lower plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-test performance can peak early during noisy multi-label training, with trajectories depending on the training method.

record.peer_reviewed: Asian Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 189, 2022
record.problems: No random-label or unstructured-input tests; no training-set error results; most cross-noise curves are figure-only; no uncertainty estimates are reported. V6's real-pattern-first account is not directly measured and is partly attributed to cited prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No substantive eligible reported outcomes omitted. Intermediate values in Figure 4 and plotted epoch values in Figures 4(d) and 5(b) were not transcribed because they are figure-only. The full Table 1 was preserved only where explicit text gives a value; other flattened cells could not be reliably assigned to the trusted-data rows.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit across noise fractions, progression to fully random labels and chance performance, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization. Only clean-test degradation under 0–60% corruption is measured.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and of their removal on true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for real patterns and corrupted labels; clean-test trajectories alone do not establish their learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of training-fit and label-specific learning measurements is an untested component, not evidence warranting limits_scope. The supplied Table 1 can be aligned: ASL and MPVAE occupy the first two numerical rows, followed by TLCM with 5%, 10%, and 15% trusted data.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling experiment or chance-level test error measurement.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or convergence across corrupted-label fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

Tests symmetric label noise only at selected fractions and reports test-set mAP, CF1 and OF1. Does not establish perfect training-set fit or separately measure capture of remaining signal versus memorization.
Does not test weight decay, dropout or data augmentation, or their removal.
Reports performance over epochs at 40% noise, but does not directly compare when shared real-data patterns versus noisy labels are learned, and does not test completely random labels.

tranche.reason: The study uses the memorization account to motivate noise mitigation and reports clean-test performance. It does not measure fitting random training labels or separately track learning clean and corrupted labels.

source_check.notes: R22 duplicates the TLCM trajectory summarized in R23. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased; their interpretation of test-mAP trajectories does not establish V6's clean-before-noisy label-learning order.
